0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 1986, after the draft finalized by the Institution on 15 December Stimulant Foods Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council.

0.2 Quality estimation of `Cocoa mass' assumes importance, because it is marketed as a finished product and is used as a major ingredient/raw material in the manufacture of chocolate, chocolate coating, cocoa beverages, bakery goods and confectionery. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordThe number of significant places retained in ance with IS : 2-1960*. the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value of this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard
prescribes and test for cocoa mass. the requirements and method of sampling

2. REQUIREMENTS

2.1 Description

- Cocoa mass shall be a solid or semisolid material prepared by adequate grinding of commercially shell free nibs ( cotyledons ) of well fermented, dried and roasted cocoa beans, the seeds of Thcobroma cacoa.
2.2 The product shall have its characteristic coIour, odour and flavour and it shall be free from any added colouring matter, flavour, preservative, adulterants, harmful ingredients, or added fats other than Cocoa butter. *Rules for rounding off numerical values ( mised). 3

2.4 Optional Treatment and Ingredients - The material may at any stage during its manufacture be treated with alkalizing agents, such as hydroxides, carbonates and bicarbonates of sodium, potassium, magnesium and aluminium only not exceeding 5 percent singly or in combination and expressed as anhydrous potassium carbonate on fat free basis. F-2. PROCEDURE F-2.1 Preparation of Moisture and Fat Free Material - Treat 7 g of the prepared sample ( A-l.1 ) in a centrifuge bottle twice, with 100 ml of ether. Centrifuge and decant superanatant liquid after each addition of ether. Dry the residue in an air-oven at 100 f 2�C and powder it with a flattened glass rod. Wash with 100 ml of water centrifuge for 10 minutes and decant the aqueous alcohol twice and with 100 ml of ether once, in the same manner as with water. Transfer the moisture and fat-free residue to a dish and dry it to constant weight in an air-oven at 105�C. Use this for the determination of crude fibre ( F-2.2 ). F-2.2 Weigh accurately above 2.5 g of the residue ( F-2.1 ) and transfer to a litre flask. Take 200 ml of dilute sulphuric acid in a beaker and Transfer the whole of the boiling acid to the flask bring to the boil. containing the residue and immediateIy connect the flask with a reflux water condenser and heat, so that the contents of the flask begin to boil within one minute. Rotate the flask frequently, taking care to keep the *Specification for ether ( second rcoision ). *Specification for absolutealcohol `, revised ). 11

IS:11923-1986
material from remaining on the sides of the flask out of contact with the acid. Continue boiling for exactly 30 minutes. Remove the flask and filter through fine linen ( about 18 threads to a centimetre ) held in a funnel, and wash with boiling water until the washings are no longer acid Heat some quantity of sodium hydroxide solution to boiling to litmus. Wash the residue on the linen into the flask under a reflux condenser. Immediately with 200 ml of the boiling sodium hydroxide solution. connect the flask with the reflux condenser and boil for exactly Remove the flask and immediately filter through the filter30 minutes. Thoroughly wash the residue with boiling water and transfer ing cloth. to a Gooch crucible prepared with a thin but compact layer of the ignited asbestos ( F-l.6 ). Wash the residue thoroughly first with hot water and then with about 15 ml of ethylalcohol, 95 percent by volume. Dry the Gooch crucible and contents at 105�C in an air-oven to constant weight, Cool and weigh. Incinerate the contents of the Gooch crucible in a muffle furnace at 600 f 20�C until all the carbonaceous matter is burnt. Cool the Gooch crucible containing the ash in a desiccator and weigh. F-3. APPENDIX G [ Table 1, Item (viii) ]
DETERMINATION G-l. APPARATUS OF PARTICLE SIZE

G-l.1 Sieve - The sieve comprises a 7.5 cm diameter hollow cylinder of tinned copper 6 cm high to which is a long hoop. The base of the sieve is flanged and covered with standard wire gauze, 150 mesh, and soldered all round the edge. A metal ring is soldered on the lower side of the gauge to protect the sieve when standing on the bench.

The sampling jnxwmnent shall be clean and dry when used. 13

H-l.3 Precautions shall be taken to protect the samples, the material being sampled, the sampling instrument and containers for samples from adventitious contaminationH-l.4 The samples shall be placed in clean and dry glass containers. The sample containers shall be of such a size that they are almost completely filled by the sample. H-l.5 Each container shall be sealed air-tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, batch or code number, name of the manufacturer and other important particulars of the consignment. H-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING

H-2.1 Lot - All the containers in a single consignment of the material drawn from a single batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. H-2.1.1 From each lot, conformity of the material. samples shall be tested to ascertain the

H-2.2 The number of containers to be selected randomly. Selection shall depend on the size N of the lot and shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 2.

H-3. PREPARATION SAMPLE

OF TEST

SAMPLES

AND REFEREE

H-3.1 About 250 g of the material shall be taken from each of the selected containers after melting the contents at 55�C and mixing them thoroughly with a sampling tube. H-3.2 Preparation of Composite Sample - Equal quantities of material ( about 100 g ) shall be taken from the sample as obtained in H-3.1 and mixed thoroughly to constitute a composite sample of size 300 g. This sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, one for the vendor and the third one for the referee. The test samples so obtained shall be transferred immediately to thoroughly These shall be labelled clean and dry containers and sealed air-tight. with particulars of sampling given in H-1.5. 14

IS:11923

-1986

H-3.3 Preparation of lndividual Sample - The remaining portions of the material from each of the selected containers ( after thi! required quantity needed for formation of the composite sample ) shall be divided These parts shall be immediately transferred to into three equal parts. thoroughly dried containers which are then sealed air-tight and labelled with all the particulars given in G-1.5. H-3.4 Referee Sampleb - Referee samples shall consist of the composite sample ( see H-3.2 ) and a set of individual test samples ( see H-3.3 ) marked for this purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. These shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two. H-4. NUMBER OF TESTS

H-4.1 The test for the description, total fat, total ash, acid insoluble ash, alkalinity of ash, and crude fibre shall be conducted on the individual samples as obtained in H-3.3. H-4.2 The test for remaining characteristics composite sample as prepared under H-3.2. H-5. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY of this shall be made in the

H-5.1 A lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements standard if H-5.1.1 and H-5.1.2 are satisfied.

H-5.1.1 Each of the test results obtained for various characteristics from individual testing ( see H-4) shall satisfy the corresponding requirements as given in 2.
